serp_review.query: gmail delete promotions older than 30 days keep recent
serp_review.observation: A standard web search returned general 'delete all promotions' guides (novocall, inquirer, androidauthority, incogni, clean.email, gizchina, getinboxzero). None gave a combined category:promotions older_than:30d recipe with a keep preview; one suggested using the search-options date field and another suggested filters for ongoing cleanup without addressing that filters cannot act on age. None covered rescuing receipts filed as promotions, mixed conversations, archived mail missing from the tab, or the difference between the search cutoff and the Trash 30-day period.
serp_review.limitation: A single standard search, US results only; not a full Google SERP capture. A follow-up search for official 'Date within' documentation found none, so the draft omits the search-options date field.

information_gain: A five-row search table for this exact job (delete, keep preview, receipt rescue with documented {} OR syntax, fixed-date alternative, 30d vs 1m) each with what it can miss; a rescue-before-delete step for receipts and return labels filed as promotions; an explicit explanation of why an older_than filter cannot act as a 30-day expiry; the archived-mail gap between the Promotions tab and search (quoted from Google); and the 'two 30-day clocks' clarification separating the search cutoff from Trash permanent deletion. Published owners cover this in one line each (hub: category:promotions older_than:1y; promotions guide: category:promotions older_than:6m).
overlap_check: Hub how-to-delete-emails-older-than-a-year-gmail owns general age cleanup and has one promotions row; gmail-delete-all-promotional-emails owns clearing the whole category and has one older_than:6m line; gmail-filters-delete-emails-automatically owns incoming-rule setup and its age-filter paragraph is linked rather than repeated. Draft gmail-delete-from-sender-keep-recent is the sender analogue; this draft shares the step shape but its table, rescue step, archive note and Trash-clock section are category-specific.
limitations: Source and documentation review only; no live Gmail mailbox test was run and no screenshots were produced.
Length of an 'm' month and inclusiveness of before:/after: are undocumented; the table warns rather than stating behaviour.
Whether category:promotions search includes archived mail is undocumented and untested; the draft says so.
That moving a message to Primary removes it from category:promotions results is inferred, and the reader is told to verify by rerunning.
The claim that list selection acts on whole conversations is inferred from Google's separate 'Delete this message' option.
That the Trash 30 days run from the trash date is the natural reading of Google's text, not a quoted statement.
The fixed-date example before:2026/09/19 is 30 days before the draft date and will look stale later.
The rescue search matches words only; receipts without 'receipt', 'order' or 'invoice' are missed, as the draft states.
Google pages cited are the computer variants; mobile app behaviour was not reviewed.
